A 7 year old child inmate of the British concentration camp at Bloemfontein, who died from typhoid fever during the Second Boer War. Present day South Africa. 1901 (NSFW)

This image is of a seven year old Boer girl named Lizzie Van Zyl (1894 – 9 May 1901), who was a child inmate of Bloemfontein concentration camp during the Second Boer War. She later died in the concentration camp of typhoid fever.

The British incarcerated her in the camp following the refusal of her father, a Boer combatant, to surrender. The photo of the emaciated van Zyl reportedly was passed from pro-War author Arthur Conan Doyle, who was serving as a volunteer doctor, to English politician Joseph Chamberlain. It was then used as propaganda to convince the British public that Boer children were neglected by their parents as it was said that the picture was taken when they were admitted to the camp, when in fact it was taken some time later..
